If a reported data-record error concerns a record starting on physical line 5, the error contains the number 5.
verdicts.missing: Whether the result lists every failing row with its reason or stops at the first failing row.

verdicts.quote: Submitting a record with an identity already present in the applicable scope reports a conflict for that record ... Submitting two records with the same new identity reports a conflict within the file.
An admin cannot assign rights through import that ordinary user creation would prohibit that admin from assigning.
An admin with user-creation authority submits a CSV file through the product.
verdicts.missing: Whether bulk import is a distinct permission; the spec ties it to user-creation authority rather than stating it is not implied by it.

verdicts.quote: A file with user values as its first nonempty record and no header is rejected. ... A header containing an unrecognized field is rejected. ... Omitting that column fails the check.

Adding a UTF-8 byte order mark ... does not change ... the import outcome. ... LF or CRLF record endings have equivalent outcomes. ... a quoted field containing a comma ... or a line break imports as one field
after creation work has begun, none of its proposed users remain from that attempt. ... its proposed users receive no such notifications from that submission.
A file of 1,048,577 bytes fails it. ... A file with 1,001 user records below the byte ceiling fails that check. ... A limit rejection tells the admin the maximum for the exceeded measurement.
A zero-byte file, a file containing only empty lines, and a header-only file each fail with an outcome indicating the absence of user records. ... A valid one-record submission creates its user.
The admin resubmits a file whose accounts are all still present. No second account is created for any of those identities.
If ordinary creation requires an onboarding notification for an account in the same state, the imported user receives the corresponding notification after the account is created.
verdicts.missing: Whether up to 1,000 notifications go out at once and any pacing or throttling of them.

verdicts.quote: A newly imported user starts in the same initial account state as a comparable ordinarily created user ... the imported user must complete that step before gaining access.
If ordinary user creation is required to produce an audit record, a reviewer can find the required audit information for a user created by import.
verdicts.missing: An audit of the import itself: who uploaded which file and when, independent of existing per-user creation audit requirements.
